skill.name: toon-format
skill.description: Encode structured data in TOON, a compact notation for LLM prompts that can reduce tokens compared with JSON.
skill.summary: Creates and validates compact TOON representations for structured LLM prompt data.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown formatting, syntax examples, documentation URLs, or harmless /dev/null redirection. Real risk remains where the skill directs agents to run npx validation and Python repair scripts, especially with AUTO_FIX enabled by default.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is part of the normal workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx @toon-format/cli, and pin the package version in examples.

remediation.issue: Automatic repair scripts can modify files under a supplied path.
remediation.suggestion: Set AUTO_FIX to false by default, document dry-run behavior, and require the user to approve the target path before changes.

remediation.issue: Online tooling links may lead users to paste sensitive structured data into third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to avoid uploading confidential data to playgrounds unless the user has approval.

content.value_statement: JSON can waste tokens when repeated structured data is sent to AI models. This skill helps convert suitable data into compact TOON with validation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains when TOON is appropriate for repeated structured data.
Formats key-value pairs, arrays, nested objects, and tabular records.
Requires explicit array counts and two-space row indentation.
Provides rules for escaping multiline strings and nested cell values.
Recommends CLI validation and lists common automatic repair steps.
Shows token comparison examples between JSON and TOON.
limitations: TOON is not recommended for deeply nested or highly irregular data.
Validation depends on an external CLI package when strict mode is used.
Automatic repair guidance may modify files if run without review.
JSON should remain the canonical format for tool-read configuration files.

use_cases.title: Compress Prompt Data
use_cases.description: Convert repeated records into compact TOON before sending them to a model.

use_cases.title: Build Documentation Indexes
use_cases.description: Represent page summaries, metadata, and keyword lists in a concise tabular form.

use_cases.title: Review Structured Records
use_cases.description: Prepare repeated business or product records for AI review while keeping JSON as the source.

prompt_templates.title: Encode a Simple Table
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion from a small list of records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this list of records into TOON. Use explicit counts, two-space row indentation, and a blank line after each table.

prompt_templates.title: Check TOON Validity
prompt_templates.scenario: Review existing TOON for common format mistakes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TOON content for syntax problems. List each issue and provide a corrected version using the skill rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design a TOON Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a compact representation before writing data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TOON structure for this dataset. Explain which fields should be tabular and which should stay as nested values.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Conversion Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with validation and source preservation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to convert JSON source data into TOON for model prompts. Include validation, repair steps, and rules for preserving the canonical source.

output_examples.input: A repeated list of users with identifiers, names, and email addresses.
output_examples.output: A compact TOON table with an explicit row count, named columns, indented rows, and a terminating blank line.

output_examples.input: A documentation page summary with metadata, concepts, warnings, and one short code pattern.
output_examples.output: A TOON page summary that keeps metadata as key-value fields and repeated concepts as counted arrays.

output_examples.input: A TOON file that fails validation because rows are not indented and comments are present.
output_examples.output: A concise fix list that removes comments, indents table rows, and recommends CLI validation after review.

best_practices: Use TOON for repeated records and keep JSON as the canonical source.
Validate generated TOON before relying on it in production prompts.
Review any automatic file fixes before applying them to a repository.
anti_patterns: Do not use TOON for deeply nested data that changes schema often.
Do not omit array counts or table row indentation.
Do not paste sensitive data into online playgrounds without approval.

faq.question: What is TOON used for?
faq.answer: TOON represents structured data in a compact form for AI prompts, especially repeated records.

faq.question: Does this replace JSON?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends keeping JSON as the canonical source and using TOON for model transport.

faq.question: Can it handle nested objects?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill recommends JSON for deeply nested or irregular structures.

faq.question: How does validation work?
faq.answer: The skill recommends decoding TOON with the official CLI to confirm the format is valid.

faq.question: Can the repair steps change files?
faq.answer: Yes. The automatic repair scripts operate on paths, so users should review scope before running them.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
